status: PARTIALLY PINNED — 6/19 claims (capacity 2/7, speed 4/12) — filled by make-engine-identity.py; re-audit on every re-pin
why: A digest-pinned image says which manifest was pulled. It does not say which BYTES ran: the recipe bind-mounts patched engine files over the image's own, and the capacity profile installs a pinned b12x build on top of the baked one. The build stamp and the engine-critical file hashes say that. This manifest ships PARTLY FILLED on purpose: what can be computed without an image is computed here (the build stamps, and the digests of the patch files this repository itself ships), and what cannot — the image-baked engine files — is left as a <FILL-IN: ...> marker, because an invented digest is worse than no digest. Fill the rest with make-engine-identity.py (one command, against a container that is already up) and the boot gate becomes a real adoption gate: a re-pinned image fails it until it is re-audited. A pinned digest carries no inline description, so files_why gives its provenance; an unfilled claim keeps its description in the marker itself.
how_to_fill: python3 launch/tp3-kit/make-engine-identity.py --profile speed --container ds4flash-tp3-head --write   (run on the box that owns the container, then re-stage the kit; --profile capacity for the capacity profile)
not_pinned_marker: any value that is not a 64-character lowercase sha256 digest is treated as NOT PINNED: the gate reports it per claim and the default run passes, so a fresh clone boots. --strict turns every unpinned claim into a FAIL, so a strict run can never pass on a manifest that pins nothing.

The DISTRIBUTION version the container reports is the commit id plus the nightly's packaging date — 0.1.dev21553+gab86b7073.d20261004 — and the gate compares the distribution version exactly, so that is what is pinned here; the README stack table publishes the same string. make-engine-identity.py records what your container actually reports.

files_why.vllm/model_executor/kernels/mhc/tilelang: bind-mounted dynamo-safe probe — the bytes are this repository's own patches/tilelang.py, mounted over the image's copy by launch/ds4flash-tp3-spark. It is based on the engine file as it stood BEFORE the upstream 'Route DeepSeek hc head through TileLang op' commit, so a capacity boot runs the older routing — see NOTICE. The capacity profile mounts it whenever it has been staged; a container holding the image's own copy instead is a DIFFERENT routing than the recipe audited, and this digest is what makes that visible.
